title: Size overflow and boundaries
goal: Check a byte-size product by division before performing the multiplication.

prerequisites.text: Know size_t and why to bound element counts.
Know the distinction between zero and positive divisors.

terms.title: Maximum size
terms.definition: SIZE_MAX is the largest size_t value in the current environment.

terms.title: Size product
terms.definition: The number of bytes obtained by multiplying the element count by the width of one element.

terms.title: Output parameter
terms.definition: A pointer to a result variable. The function updates bytes only on success.

sections.title: Check before multiplying
paragraphs: When count and width are positive, the maximum valid count is SIZE_MAX / width. Compare with that bound before multiplying.
With width = 0, that bound calculation cannot divide by width. The first check therefore ensures a positive divisor. A zero count is outside this task's contract as well.

An out-of-range product computed in an unsigned type wraps and can become small. Check the size before multiplying. This lesson does not allocate memory. The caller passes the address of a live bytes variable, and the function writes the result only on success.

sections.title: Check a large count without allocating
paragraphs: For all three calls, predict the status and whether the output variable bytes changes.
steps: 4 and 3 are positive and are within the bound. The function stores 12.
SIZE_MAX exceeds SIZE_MAX / 2. The function returns overflow before multiplying.
With width = 0 the function exits before division.

sections.title: Locate and check the defect
paragraphs: The diagnostic called object type is not a function shows that bytes was incorrectly written as bytes(). Pass the bytes value to %zu. Use &bytes when passing the output argument to bytes_for.
If the overflowing case is classified as invalid, the program has lost the distinction between failure categories. The overflow status tests the representational bound without any allocation.

sections.title: Change, predict and check
paragraphs: Compare widths 1 and 2 with count = SIZE_MAX. The product is representable at width 1. The check rejects width 2. Explain the difference without calculating SIZE_MAX.
For width 2 compare count = SIZE_MAX / 2 and count = SIZE_MAX / 2 + 1. The second count is representable, but its product with the width is out of range. Do not compute the rejected product.

reading.author: ISO/IEC JTC1/SC22/WG14
reading.title: ISO/IEC 9899:2018 — Programming languages — C
reading.purpose: Review the language and library contracts used in this example.

selfcheck.prompt: When may bytes be read as the resulting size?
feedback: Success guarantees that a result was written.
On failure the value remains untouched.
Overflow prevents both computation and assignment.

options: Accept it as a safe size
feedback: The check protects the division operation.

selfcheck.prompt: Why does overflow on input -1 2 establish a computation guard rather than a malloc failure?
selfcheck.feedback: Mode -1 2 passes SIZE_MAX and 2 into a pure size check. It never calls malloc.

practice.title: Calculate capacity in bytes
practice.task: The first line, at most 63 bytes, contains count 0–16 and width 0–8. The special teaching input -1 2 passes SIZE_MAX and 2 to the size check without asking for a large integer. Every other pair with -1 is invalid. Print bytes N for a positive representable product, overflow for an out-of-range product, and invalid for zero or malformed input. This exercise allocates no memory.
criteria: 3 4 gives bytes 12, 16 8 gives bytes 128, and 0 4 gives invalid.
-1 2 yields overflow before multiplication and without allocation.
practice.hint: After checking width, compare count with SIZE_MAX / width. Store a result only on the validated path.

steps.action: Run the starter with 3 4 and separately with -1 2. Find both TODOs in bytes_for.
steps.why: The starter stores count instead of the product and does not distinguish the two failure types.
steps.expected: The results are bytes 3 and invalid respectively.

steps.action: Fix the status and product assignment. Run 3 4, 3 0, and -1 2 separately.
steps.why: The mode -1 2 selects SIZE_MAX without an allocation request.
steps.expected: The results are bytes 12, invalid, and overflow respectively.

exercises.title: Transfer the idea
exercises.task: In a separate check set bytes = 99 and call bytes_for with width 2 and count = SIZE_MAX / 2. Reset bytes to 99 and call again with count = SIZE_MAX / 2 + 1. Do not allocate memory.
criteria: The first status is BYTES_OK and the product is stored. The second status is SIZE_OVERFLOW and bytes remains 99.
